Resource `azapi_resource` supports `ignore_changes`

Add a new field `ignore_changes` to the resource `azapi_resource` to allow users to ignore the changes of the resource.

**Example 1**

There're resources could be managed by two sets of APIs, for example, "Microsoft.Network/virtualNetworks/subnets" could be managed by its own API and by the virtualNetworks API.

In the following config, the first apply could create the vnet and the subnet. But in the next apply, because there's no definition in the vnet's subnet definition, the vnet will update the resource and remove all subnets.

After adding the `ignore_changes` to the vnet, the vnet will not update the subnets.

```hcl
resource "azapi_resource" "vnet" {
  type = "Microsoft.Network/virtualNetworks@2020-06-01"
  ...

  ignore_changes = [
    "properties.subnets",
  ]
}

resource "azapi_resource" "subnet" {
  type = "Microsoft.Network/virtualNetworks/subnets@2020-06-01"
  ....
}


```

azapi_resource: `RequiresReplace` / `taint` / `-replace` silently demoted to in-place update by `ModifyPlan`

## Summary

On `azapi_resource`, a planned replacement — whether requested by `terraform taint`, `terraform plan -replace=...`, the custom `RequiresReplaceIfNotNull` plan modifier on `replace_triggers_external_values`, or the imperative `response.RequiresReplace.Append(...)` calls inside the resource's own `ModifyPlan` (for `location`, `replace_triggers_refs`) — is silently demoted to an in-place update (or a no-op). The Azure resource is never destroyed; it is only PUT-updated.

Only `name` and `parent_id` reliably trigger a replace, because they change the Azure resource ID and therefore the `id` attribute, which Terraform sees as a diff regardless of what `ModifyPlan` does.

## Root cause

In [`internal/services/azapi_resource.go` lines 541–548](https://github.com/Azure/terraform-provider-azapi/blob/main/internal/services/azapi_resource.go#L541-L548), `ModifyPlan` installs an **unconditional deferred write-back** of the plan struct:

```go
defer func() {
    if plan.Output.IsUnknown() {
        plan.Body = config.Body
        plan.Type = config.Type
    }
    response.Plan.Set(ctx, plan)
}()
```

Before that deferred `response.Plan.Set` fires, the same function mutates several non-computed plan fields back toward state:

| File:line | Mutation |
|---|---|
| `azapi_resource.go:553` | `plan.Output = state.Output` |
| `azapi_resource.go:584` | `plan.Identity = state.Identity` (when semantically equal) |
| `azapi_resource.go:629-630` | `plan.Body = state.Body; plan.Type = state.Type` (when `IgnoreNoOpChanges` is on and remote body matches config) |
| `azapi_resource.go:662`   | `plan.Tags = r.tagsWithDefaultTags(...)` re-derived from state |
| `azapi_resource.go:668`   | `plan.Location = r.locationWithDefaultLocation(...)` re-derived/normalised from state |

After these normalisations, the re-encoded `plan` written back by `response.Plan.Set(ctx, plan)` is byte-for-byte identical to the prior state for every attribute. Terraform then computes "planned new state == prior state ⇒ NoOp" and **collapses the plan**, dropping the replace markers with it. The `RequiresReplace` decoration alone is not sufficient — the framework still collapses the plan when there is no actual attribute diff between state and the rewritten planned new state.

The pre-Create existence guard at [`azapi_resource.go:810-830`](https://github.com/Azure/terraform-provider-azapi/blob/main/internal/services/azapi_resource.go#L810-L830) (GET → error "Resource already exists") **would** catch a skipped-Delete case, but because the replace is collapsed to NoOp/Update, that guard never runs.

## Impact

Any workflow that relies on replacement being actually performed is broken on `azapi_resource`:

- `terraform taint azapi_resource.foo` followed by `terraform apply` — no destroy.
- `terraform apply -replace=azapi_resource.foo` — no destroy.
- The schema's own `replace_triggers_external_values` (when nothing else changes).
- The schema's own `replace_triggers_refs` (handled at `azapi_resource.go:711`).
- The `location` change replacement appended at `azapi_resource.go:671`.
- Any downstream module using `lifecycle { replace_triggered_by = [...] }` pointing at an `azapi_resource`.

For resources where the delete semantics actually matter (e.g. resources holding non-idempotent state on the Azure side, resources whose `type` or `body` schema changed in a way a PUT can't express cleanly), users silently get an in-place PUT instead of the destroy+create they asked for.

## Reproduction

```hcl
resource "azapi_resource" "example" {
  type      = "Microsoft.Resources/resourceGroups@2021-04-01"
  name      = "example-rg"
  location  = "westeurope"
  parent_id = "/subscriptions/<sub-id>"
  body      = {}
}
```

```
terraform apply            # creates
terraform taint azapi_resource.example
terraform plan             # expected: 1 to destroy, 1 to add
                           # actual:   No changes.  (or at most an in-place update)
```

Same behaviour with `terraform apply -replace=azapi_resource.example`.

## Related commits

- `df654e197` — `fix: RequiresReplaceIfNotNull handles typed null from HCL conditional expressions (#1070)`
- `73edff495` — `fix(planmodifier): requires replace external values should not replace if state value is null (#866)`
- `c01b368d4` — `bugfix: don't replace the resource if API returns readonly location (#845)`

These fixed specific plan-modifier edge cases, but the underlying clobber in `ModifyPlan` means that even when the plan modifier correctly appends to `response.RequiresReplace`, the change is erased.

## Proposed fix

Guard the deferred write-back (and the `IgnoreNoOpChanges` body-reset) so they never run when a replace has been scheduled. Minimum patch on `azapi_resource.go`:

```go
defer func() {
    // Don't overwrite the plan if a replace has been scheduled - our
    // field-level normalisations (identity/tags/location/body/type etc.)
    // would otherwise collapse the diff and silently demote the replace
    // to a no-op update.
    if len(response.RequiresReplace) > 0 {
        return
    }
    if plan.Output.IsUnknown() {
        plan.Body = config.Body
        plan.Type = config.Type
    }
    response.Plan.Set(ctx, plan)
}()
```

And around the `IgnoreNoOpChanges` block (lines 591–632), skip it when `len(response.RequiresReplace) > 0`.

Note: `taint` and `-replace` propagate to the provider via `request.Plan.Raw.IsNull()` on the destroy half of the cycle (which the existing early-return at `azapi_resource.go:537-539` already handles correctly). The failure mode described here is specifically the **plan-modifier-driven replacement path** — and, transitively, any `taint`/`-replace` call whose re-planning hits `ModifyPlan` with a non-null request plan (e.g. the re-plan step after destroy). A more complete fix should also call `response.Plan.SetAttribute(ctx, path.Root(...), value)` per mutated attribute rather than re-encoding the whole struct, so the framework's diff decorations are not erased.

## Other resources in this provider

The same `response.Plan.Set(ctx, plan)` write-back exists in the other managed resources, but today they only mutate **computed** fields (`Output`/`SensitiveOutput`) before the write-back, so they do not currently exhibit the replace-suppression bug:

- `internal/services/azapi_update_resource.go:377`
- `internal/services/azapi_data_plane_resource.go:347`
- `internal/services/azapi_resource_action_resource.go:290`

These should still be hardened (with the same `len(response.RequiresReplace) > 0` guard, or by moving to per-attribute `SetAttribute` calls) so that future non-computed mutations don't silently reintroduce the same class of bug.

## Environment

- Provider: `azapi` — reproduced against `main` (commit at time of report).
- Affected resource: `azapi_resource`.
- Terraform: any recent version (tested on 1.x).

moved from azurerm_* to azapi_resource selects an unsupported API version and drops location

### Summary

`AzapiResource.MoveState` builds the target state from the resource ID alone. It sets only `ID`, `Name`, `ParentID` and `Type`, deriving the API version from the newest embedded type rather than from anything the practitioner configured.

This produces two distinct failures when migrating an `azurerm_*` resource whose newest **embedded** API version is not served by ARM.

Unlike `terraform import`, there is **no user-facing escape hatch**: a `moved` block accepts no arguments, so the `?api-version=` workaround documented for imports (#174, #1043) cannot be applied.

### Versions

- `Azure/azapi` **v2.12.0** (latest at time of writing)
- Terraform **v1.15.8**

### Reproduction

`Microsoft.Portal/dashboards`. The provider embeds `2026-04-01`:

```
internal/azure/generated/portal/microsoft.portal/
  2015-08-01-preview  2018-10-01-preview  2019-01-01-preview
  2020-09-01-preview  2022-12-01-preview  2025-04-01-preview  2026-04-01
```

ARM does not serve `2026-04-01`:

```console
$ az provider show -n Microsoft.Portal \
    --query "resourceTypes[?resourceType=='dashboards'].apiVersions | [0]" -o tsv
2025-04-01-preview  2022-12-01-preview  2020-09-01-preview  2020-09-01-alpha
2019-01-01-preview  2018-10-01-preview  2015-08-01-preview
```

Given an existing `azurerm_portal_dashboard` in state, migrate it:

```hcl
resource "azapi_resource" "this" {
  type      = "Microsoft.Portal/dashboards@2019-01-01-preview"
  name      = "example"
  parent_id = "/subscriptions/<sub>/resourceGroups/<rg>"
  location  = "eastus"
  body      = { properties = { lenses = {} } }
}

moved {
  from = azurerm_portal_dashboard.dashboard
  to   = azapi_resource.this
}
```

### Failure 1 — plan is blocked

```
Error: Failed to retrieve resource

  with azapi_resource.this,

reading Resource: (ResourceId
"/subscriptions/.../providers/Microsoft.Portal/dashboards/example"
/ Api Version "2026-04-01"): GET https://management.azure.com/...
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
RESPONSE 400: 400 Bad Request
ERROR CODE: NoRegisteredProviderFound
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
{
  "error": {
    "code": "NoRegisteredProviderFound",
    "message": "No registered resource provider found for location 'eastus' and API version '2026-04-01' for type 'dashboards'. The supported api-versions are '2015-08-01-preview, 2018-10-01-preview, 2019-01-01-preview, 2020-09-01-preview, 2020-09-01-alpha, 2022-12-01-preview, 2025-04-01-preview'. ..."
  }
}
```

The configured `type` is `2019-01-01-preview`. The error names `2026-04-01`, which appears nowhere in the configuration, and nothing in the message points at `moved`, at state migration, or at the provider's embedded types.

The upgrade cannot proceed. State is not corrupted — the move is not persisted, and `terraform state list` still shows the original `azurerm_portal_dashboard` address.

### Failure 2 — `-refresh=false` silently becomes destructive

`-refresh=false` is a natural reaction to a refresh-time error, and it converts the hard failure into a destroy/recreate:

```
  # azapi_resource.this must be replaced
  # (moved from azurerm_portal_dashboard.dashboard)
-/+ resource "azapi_resource" "this" {
      + location = "eastus" # forces replacement
      ~ type     = "Microsoft.Portal/dashboards@2026-04-01" -> "Microsoft.Portal/dashboards@2019-01-01-preview"
    }

Plan: 4 to add, 0 to change, 1 to destroy.
```

`MoveState` never populates `location`, and `location` forces replacement. The post-move refresh is normally the only thing that backfills it, so suppressing refresh removes the sole guardrail.

### Root cause

https://github.com/Azure/terraform-provider-azapi/blob/main/internal/services/azapi_resource.go

```go
id, err := parse.ResourceID(azureId)

state := NewDefaultAzapiResourceModel()
state.ID       = types.StringValue(id.ID())
state.Name     = types.StringValue(id.Name)
state.ParentID = types.StringValue(id.ParentId)
state.Type     = types.StringValue(fmt.Sprintf("%s@%s", id.AzureResourceType, id.ApiVersion))
```

All four values derive from the parsed ID. An ARM resource ID encodes subscription, resource group, provider namespace, type and name — but **not** `location`, so `location` is left null. `id.ApiVersion` falls back to the newest embedded version because the `azurerm` ID carries none.

`location` cannot be inferred from the resource group either, since a resource may live in a different region than its parent RG.

### Impact

Only affects migrations of existing state; greenfield deployments are unaffected.

Severity scales with the resource type. `moved` blocks from `azurerm_*` to `azapi_resource` ship today in Azure Verified Modules for, among others, `azurerm_storage_account` and `azurerm_private_endpoint` — both location-bearing. For those, a user who works around Failure 1 with `-refresh=false` gets a destroy/recreate of a stateful resource.

Because the check is location-scoped and depends on the gap between the embedded types and ARM rollout, the same configuration can succeed in one region and fail in another, or begin failing after an `azapi` upgrade bumps the embedded default. Sovereign clouds, where API versions lag, are more exposed.

### Suggested fixes

**1. Populate `location` (and `tags`) from the source state.**
`SourceRawState` is always available and the `azurerm` state already contains them — `azurerm_portal_dashboard`, for example, declares `"location": commonschema.Location()` as required. The current `SourceSchema` only requests `id`, `resource_manager_id`, `resource_id` and `resource_versionless_id`, so these values are discarded today. This alone removes the destructive failure mode.

**2. Stop hard-selecting the newest embedded API version.**
Either fall back to the newest version ARM reports as supported, or retry the post-move read with the next-newest embedded version on `NoRegisteredProviderFound` — the approach suggested in #1089.

> **Note for implementers:** `MoveStateRequest` exposes `SourceState`, `SourceRawState`, `SourceTypeName` and `SourcePrivate`, but **not** the target resource's configuration. So "use the configured `type`'s API version" is not implementable inside `MoveState`; fix 2 needs to work without it.

Regenerating the embedded types will not help here — the embedded version is *ahead* of the deployed service rather than stale, which distinguishes this from #1043 and #1089.

### Related

- #174 — `import` ignores the API version in `type`; mitigated by `?api-version=`
- #1043 — `import` uses an unsupported API version
- #1089 — same, with a suggestion to fall back on `NoRegisteredProviderFound`

All three concern the `import` path, where `?api-version=` provides a workaround. No equivalent exists for `moved`.

# Support dynamic, value-driven `ignore_changes` in `azapi_resource`

## Use case (generic module development)

When building reusable Terraform modules on top of `azapi_resource`, module authors cannot expose ignore behaviour as a configurable input. Terraform's `lifecycle.ignore_changes` meta-argument only accepts a **static list of literal attribute paths** — it cannot reference variables, locals, or computed values. For generic module development this means:

- A module cannot let its consumers opt in or out of ignoring specific body fields (for example properties mutated out-of-band by Azure Policy, autoscalers, or other controllers).
- Authors must hard-code ignore paths, forcing one-size-fits-all behaviour that produces spurious diffs for some consumers and drift for others.
- The classic case is **tags**: some consumers want them managed externally and ignored, others want them enforced by the module. With a static `ignore_changes` there is no clean way to make this a module input.

AzAPI previously offered `ignore_body_changes`, which gave dynamic, value-driven control over which parts of the request body were ignored. Its deprecation (#583) removed the only mechanism that let module authors **parameterise** this behaviour, so a provider-native dynamic equivalent is needed.

## High-level implementation options

1. **Reinstate a dynamic body-ignore argument.** Provide a regular provider argument (e.g. `ignore_changes` / `ignore_body_changes`) that accepts a list of JSON body paths sourced from a variable. Because it is a normal argument rather than a meta-argument, it can reference variables/locals and can therefore be driven by module inputs.
2. **Path-expression based ignore.** Accept JMESPath/path expressions over the resource body, evaluated by the provider at plan time, again as a dynamic-capable argument so module authors can compose the ignore set from configuration.

## Example configuration

```hcl
# Inside a reusable module
variable "ignore_changes" {
  type        = list(string)
  default     = []
  description = "JSON body paths the module consumer wants Terraform to ignore (e.g. [\"tags\", \"properties.encryption\"])."
}

resource "azapi_resource" "example" {
  type      = "Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts@2023-01-01"
  name      = var.name
  parent_id = var.resource_group_id

  body = {
    properties = {
      minimumTlsVersion = "TLS1_2"
    }
    tags = var.tags
  }

  # Proposed: a dynamic, variable-driven ignore list.
  # This is NOT possible today with lifecycle.ignore_changes, which only
  # accepts a static list of literal paths and rejects variables/locals.
  ignore_changes = var.ignore_changes
}
```

```hcl
# Consumer A — let an external process manage tags
module "storage" {
  source         = "./modules/storage"
  name           = "examplesa"
  ignore_changes = ["tags"]
}

# Consumer B — enforce everything (default behaviour, nothing ignored)
module "storage" {
  source = "./modules/storage"
  name   = "examplesa"
}
```

## Note on the underlying gap

The root cause is a gap in **Terraform core** — the `lifecycle.ignore_changes` meta-argument cannot be dynamic (it rejects variables and computed values). This has been raised upstream repeatedly with **no traction from IBM (HashiCorp)** toward a fix. A provider-side solution in AzAPI is therefore the pragmatic path forward.

*Related:* Azure/terraform-provider-azapi#583 (Deprecation of `ignore_body_changes`).

`azapi_resource` fails to read resources when Azure API returns UTF-8 BOM in JSON response

## Description

We're managing Azure Peering resources (`Microsoft.Peering/peerings`) via `azapi_resource` and since yesterday all plan/apply operations fail with:

```sh
Error: reading Resource: (ResourceId "/.../Microsoft.Peering/peerings/{name}"
/ Api Version "2025-05-01"): unmarshalling type *interface {}: invalid character 'ï'
looking for beginning of value
```

The `ï` is `0xEF` - first byte of a UTF-8 BOM (`EF BB BF`). The Azure Peering API is returning a 3 byte BOM prefix before the JSON body. Go's `encoding/json` chokes on it.

The Azure Go SDK (`azcore/runtime/response.go`) already handles this - there's a `removeBOM` function that does `bytes.TrimPrefix(b, []byte("\xef\xbb\xbf"))` before unmarshalling. But `azapi_resource` apparently doesn't go through that path. So `azurerm` would survive this just fine, but `azapi` doesn't.


## Reproduction

```bash
az rest --method GET \
  --url "https://management.azure.com/subscriptions/{sub}/resourceGroups/{rg}/providers/Microsoft.Peering/peerings/{name}?api-version=2025-05-01" \
  --output-file /tmp/peering.bin

xxd -l 4 /tmp/peering.bin
# Output: 00000000: efbb bf7b    ...{
# First 3 bytes are UTF-8 BOM, then `{` starts the JSON
```

Then any `terraform plan` on an `azapi_resource` of type `Microsoft.Peering/peerings@2025-05-01` fails during state refresh.


## Suggested fix

Strip BOM before JSON decode, same as the Go SDK already does:

```go
body = bytes.TrimPrefix(body, []byte("\xef\xbb\xbf"))
```

This would make the provider resilient to any Azure API returning BOM - not just Peering. It's a known Azure-side pattern (see Azure/msrest-for-python#144, Azure/azure-sdk-for-java#5475).

## Environment

- `azapi` provider: tested v2.5.0, v2.8.0, v2.9.0 — all fail identically
- Terraform: 1.14.3
- Terragrunt: 0.99.5
- OS: Ubuntu (GitHub Actions runner) + macOS (local)

azapi_resource: in-flight Create not preserved in state when terraform receives SIGINT (resource left orphaned in Azure)

### Summary

When `terraform apply` is interrupted with SIGINT (Ctrl+C, CI cancellation, job timeout, ...) while an `azapi_resource` is mid-Create, the resource ends up **created in Azure but absent from terraform state**. The next apply then fails with `A resource with the ID "<id>" already exists - to be managed via Terraform this resource needs to be imported`, requiring a manual `terraform import` to recover.

This is the azapi counterpart of [hashicorp/terraform-provider-azurerm#32230](https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform-provider-azurerm/issues/32230) - I confirmed the same pattern in azapi v2.9.0.

### Versions

- Terraform: `v1.14.9` on `darwin_arm64`
- Provider: `Azure/azapi v2.9.0`

### Repro

A small azapi-only config that creates a resource with a 20-30s ARM Create:

```hcl
terraform {
  required_version = "~> 1.7"
  required_providers {
    azapi = { source = "Azure/azapi", version = "~> 2.0" }
  }
}

provider "azapi" {
  subscription_id = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"
}

resource "azapi_resource" "sa" {
  type      = "Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts@2023-01-01"
  name      = "stcanceltestsample"
  location  = "westeurope"
  parent_id = "/subscriptions/00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000/resourceGroups/example-rg"

  body = {
    sku  = { name = "Standard_LRS" }
    kind = "StorageV2"
    properties = {
      accessTier               = "Hot"
      allowBlobPublicAccess    = false
      minimumTlsVersion        = "TLS1_2"
      supportsHttpsTrafficOnly = true
    }
  }
}
```

Steps:

1. `terraform apply -auto-approve`.
2. Once `azapi_resource.sa: Creating...` appears, wait ~4 seconds (so the ARM PUT has been accepted and the provider is in the poll loop).
3. Send SIGINT to the terraform process (`kill -INT <pid>` or Ctrl+C).

### Actual behaviour

Terraform exits non-zero with:

```
azapi_resource.sa: Creating...
azapi_resource.sa: Still creating... [00m10s elapsed]
Stopping operation...

Interrupt received.
Please wait for Terraform to exit or data loss may occur.
Gracefully shutting down...

Error: execution halted

Error: Failed to create/update resource

  with azapi_resource.sa,
  on main.tf line 25, in resource "azapi_resource" "sa":
  25: resource "azapi_resource" "sa" {

creating/updating Resource: (ResourceId
".../providers/Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts/stcanceltestsample"
/ Api Version "2023-01-01"): context canceled
```

After exit:

| Check                         | Result                                          |
| ----------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| `terraform state list`        | empty                                           |
| `az storage account show ...` | `provisioningState: Succeeded`, full id present |

ARM accepted the PUT and finished the create server-side, but the provider cancelled its poll context on the terraform-core Stop signal and never returned a resource id, so core had nothing to write into state. The resource is orphaned.

### Expected behaviour

On first SIGINT, terraform core asks the provider to **gracefully stop** while it flushes state (see `apparentlymart`'s walkthrough on [hashicorp/terraform#34266](https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform/issues/34266)). For an in-flight LRO Create, "graceful" should mean either:

1. Wait for the in-flight ARM Create poll to complete and return the resource id, so core can persist it (preferred for short-to-medium-running creates such as storage accounts), or
2. Persist the resource id as soon as ARM has accepted the PUT (i.e. before the poll loop completes), so even an immediate hard abort leaves a resource that can be reconciled on the next apply rather than orphaned.

Either path is far better than the current behaviour, which leaves the user with a resource in Azure but no state record and no graceful recovery short of `terraform import`.

### Notes / related

- Same pattern in azurerm: [hashicorp/terraform-provider-azurerm#32230](https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform-provider-azurerm/issues/32230). Fixes on both providers should ideally share the same approach since they face the same upstream contract.
- Same `context done` codepath family as [#1078](https://github.com/Azure/terraform-provider-azapi/issues/1078) (the **deadline** case, not the **cancel** case).
